description.value: An fMRI study investigated passive viewing and voluntary downregulation of negative emotions by reappraisal via detachment in patients with anorexia nervosa and healthy controls.

spans.text: The current functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) study investigated the hemodynamic correlates of passive viewing and voluntary downregulation of negative emotions by means of the reappraisal strategy detachment in AN patients.

description.value: Participants passively viewed negative emotional pictures for 6 seconds after a 'watch/view' cue, without trying to modulate associated feelings, followed by an arousal rating.

spans.text: During the passively viewing condition participants were instructed to simply view the picture without trying to modulate any associated feelings.

description.value: Participants viewed negative emotional pictures for 6 seconds and voluntarily downregulated their feelings using reappraisal via detachment/distancing, taking the position of a noninvolved observer, followed by an arousal rating.

spans.text: In the regulation condition they were instructed to downregulate their feeling via the reappraisal strategy ‘detachment’ (distancing), by trying to take the position of a noninvolved observer.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed either to passively view each picture without trying to modulate associated feelings ('view'/'watch') or to downregulate feelings using reappraisal via detachment ('distance'), taking the position of a noninvolved observer. After each picture, they rated current arousal.

spans.text: The instruction for each condition was given by presenting a cue word laid over the stimulus for 1.5 s stating either ‘view’ or ‘distance’.
